candidates.review_text: Last time I was here, I had the big breakfast with the salmon.  Having just spent a month on the other side of the Atlantic...I wasn't overly impressed with the smoked salmon.  I wanted something more substantial for brunch today and opted for the buttermilk fried chicken sandwich.  It was dowsed in a hot/buffalo sauce combo I believe...which was interesting.  I loved the pickle slices hidden within the brioche bun.  I was going to go crazy with the Mimosas, but the first two I ordered were so small...literally one gulp worth.  I thought about running into the nearest Anglican Cathedral for a proper glass.  I had a latte - no complaints there.  I really, really appreciate the room this place has.  The victorian lounge furniture by the fireplace upstairs - nice touch.  The booth nook is a good location.  No matter where you are, you do not feel cramped -there's space to breathe, and you aren't sitting at those flimsy glass tables that so many restaurants have these days.  A definite plus.  The people who greeted us and sat us were especially welcoming.
Definitely love the food and its excellent service. But the restaurant was so crowded. I saw customers even the waiters/waitresses had difficulties to walk through tables.

Good food, good service, inspiring presentation, but they try to pack too many people in a small space.  I sat right on top of the people next to me, who weren't at my table.  They need to expand, or get rid of a third of the tables.  Because it's usually packed, the former would be the better option.

This place has one of my favorite desserts of ALL TIME! I was in town for a conference and a friend recommended this place - we weren't able to go for dinner, however I stopped by for a quick dessert afterwards. SALTED CARAMEL BUDINO - omg! SO SO perfectly scrumptious and creamy. I loved it so much, I came back the next day for lunch, just so I could get another bite of this dessert. 

I wish I had the chance to try the dinner menu, because it is much more expansive than the lunch menu. There weren't many vegetarian options during lunch, however I managed. I ordered the truffle pizza (vegetarian). I thought it was okay - the flavor was a bit heavy for my preference. I would like to come back for dinner because there were other menu items that sounded great. I think the quality of the food and price is reasonable; I wish their lunch menu offered more though. 

The place itself is quite small and it does get very crowded; I barely felt like I had room to sit and properly enjoy my meal, however it didn't bother me that much.

Too crowded, too noisy and slow service. Other then that once getting our food, it was delicious! 

Too bad this restaurant doesn't expand because, they're always packed with customers. They must be doing something right!
The food was great except that there is not much room inside the restaurant I guess the reason is because they serve a very sumptuous meal that's why it's always crowded.

Good food and reasonable price!
The only thing I was unsatisfied is that there were too many people and it was noisy and crowded.
But every thing is fine except this.
fantastic food, ambiance, service. The only thing is that the restaurant is a little cramped and we had a table next to the door, so I got cold every time someone walked in or out.

I love all the variety you can find here. However, it is ALWAYS so crowded that it diminishes my enjoyment. I end up feeling overwhelmed and like I just need to make a choice, quick. Finding seating to eat, especially if you aren't alone, kinda sucks.

We have been to the other restaurants from the owners of Barbuzzo, so we thought to give this one a try. The restaurant is quite good, but don't expect to get a reservation day of, so plan ahead. 

The food is delicious. We had the buratta salad and the sheep's ricotta spread. The burratta is a nice. A good amount of cheese, but plenty of arugula so it is still a salad. The ricotta was soft and creamy. For entrees, we had the pizza with pear, gorgonzola, and prosciutto, and the gnocchi. Both were good. Pizzas are somewhat bigger than the other dishes if you have a larger appetite. 

Two things that the restaurant needs to work on, which will probably get ironed out in time. The first is that there is a little confusion on the concept. Is it meant to be family style or not? It is unclear from the menu and the food doesn't arrive at the same time. The second thing is that the restaurant is very cramped. I could hear the other diners' conversations a little too much at the tables on both sides of us. On one side was someone who wanted to be an actor but is doing banking instead and on the other was someone who no longer likes chai lattes. 

Overall, a good restaurant which iron out the few kinks in time.

I can't say enough good things about this place.
A wait staff that is funny and engaging, and food that is fantastic.
What more could you want from a resturant?

Crowded? Booooy howdy! Yes. This is not a place you want to casually show up to on a saturday or sunday. CALL AHEAD! For god's sake, call ahead!
But when you get in and get seated? It's totally worth it.

During the week you can pretty much come and go as you please. But lunch time, anytime, is still a packed affair. But obviously for a good reason!
A gem like this place is going to draw a crowd.

Yum.

Bone marrow: definitely an experience time thing. 2 large bones and crostini to spread the marrow on. It was good, suuuuper oily, and more than tasting good, it just looked cool.

Butternut squash: Not what we were expecting.. but we were expecting green veggies! Little fried balls.. the veggies are in this doughy batter. It's very good.

Meatballs: Actually reaaallly good. I liked them and they were delicious.

Uovo pizza: Got it because everyone else got it. I'm into the bandwagon. Not incredible but I think definitely worth trying if you've never had runny eggs on your pizza.. it's just interesting and it grows on you through the pizza, but I wouldn't order it again.

Salted caramel budino: Really good. Boyfriend loved it, I liked it a lot. I mean you obviously have to get it.. just because.

It was an overall really nice experience and I enjoyed everything, but a lot of the food was cool and novel more than it was delicious. Not that anything was bad. Also, the restaurant is mad crowded.. very small space to fit into. Which you may like or not.

I wish Tria wasn't so popular! While our choices were very good (three cheese panini, a cheese sampler, and bruschetta) and the wine and beer choices are outstanding, it is just way too crowded to enjoy everything else! 

It would be wonderful if Tria was about double the size because it's hard to imagine coming here most nights, especially on the weekend. Trying to get a drink at the bar while waiting for our table to open up was a hassle and we were constantly being squashed and run into by others trying to get a drink or the poor servers who have to make their way through the tight quarters.

Once we were seated by the window, we were able to have just enough room to eat our dinner without taking up space from those next to us. I can't say anything bad about the food or the service itself, but this place is just too crowded for me!

I don't really buy sandwiches or burger for myself because I don't enjoy eating too much meat at one sitting. I have to have lots of veggies or pickles with them. So I wasn't really expecting much when I heard praises about famous Philly cheesesteaks.

I finally tried it out when I had a trip to Philadelphia, and these are amazing! The steak is so juicy and tender and veggies in them perfectly harmonize with the meat. Nothing is overpowering but everything melts in your mouth. 

I was visiting here on Sunday afternoon and this place was packed. It's a pretty small place with around 10-15 seats. People were lining up through the door. The staff was very professional and took care of customers very quick but they weren't rude or anything. I had to wait for about 20-30 minutes to be seated but I felt like I was taken care of promptly! There are reasons for restaurants to be busy, and I could definitely see why for this place.

A classic brunch spot if you're on Penn/Drexel's campus. 

Food: Their challah French toast is a definite 5 stars and I craaaave it. The stuffed challah French toast I've also had and for someone with a sweet tooth I feel like it's overwhelming - the stuffing takes away from the perfect texture of the challah bread since it is a lot of filling and can make the plate feel borderline soggy. So I would recommend the classic! 

The savory breakfast options are also good here but I've mostly opted for the sweet - love that they have brunch specials and constantly switch out their classics for a twist with exciting new recipes. 

The other things I've tried on the brunch menu (the apple and cheddar omelette) + the long wait makes me want to give Sabrina's a 4.5. 

Ambiance: super cute and I'm-eating-in-my-grandma's home cozy kinda vibes. Lots of open space and a back area against the windows with tons of lighting. Always crowded and loud but the good busy kind of loud and not rowdy and annoying. 

Staff: most of the experience I've had with staff here has been really friendly, though because the wait is always long the host/hostess can be curt and ask you to clear the foyer area, understandable.

Did I really pay $20 for a burger? Yup. Was it the best. burger. ever.? Yup. 

I was feeling a little under the weather when I went to Village Whiskey and really was looking forward to a nice hot toddy more than anything, which didn't disappoint. I wasn't even sure about ordering food since I didn't know how well I could taste, but the hostess offered us a seat at the "back table" which turned out to be fine and we ordered burgers and fries. 

"Burgers and fries" is a total understatement. We got two orders of fries-- one with cheese and one plain. Both were delicious but the real deal here is the burgers. I ordered mine with carmelized onion and bacon. My friend got cheddar cheese and bacon. I have no idea what they do to these burgers but they are seriously gourmet. Even the rolls are rich. 

Our server was nice and helpful with questions about the menu, but service was really slow. The restaurant was definitely packed, but even ordering beers took a long time and our second order of fries took forever. 

One last note about the crowd-- definitely not what I expected. Mostly over 40 but very fun-- we were sitting in an area that was crowded with people standing and people were chatty. In retrospect and in reading other reviews, we were lucky to be seated right away. Seating is extremely limited and very cramped, even at the actual tables. Next time we will try going on a weeknight.

This restaurant was easily able to accommodate the 150 people we had for our class trip. The main floor of the restaurant was a bit cramped, with about 20 people trying to put food on their plates, and the buffet wasn't as diverse/varied as I thought it would be. However the customer service was great, the second floor was for seating but the gift shop was there too. Would possibly return again.

THIS PLACE WAS PACKED.

It was nearly impossible to safely order drinks and enjoy them(not dropping them). 

It was a fantastic atmosphere, I enjoyed the visit, but with it cold outside and hot inside, it was very uncomfortable inside smushed and crammed in.

Too crowded, so there was no way a server could give the proper attention to everyone, even though our server was great given those circumstance... My friend and I were seated at a table that would have been too small for one person, and was impossible for two.   My advice to management...stop trying to fit so many people in and concentrate more on the customers being comfortable

Revolution is a simple option if you're considering something that is akin to a Tex-Mex craving at a pretty reasonable price. I think a good comparison to their "burrito bowls" is to think about what you might order at a national chain like Chipotle (~$11). Since I am from out of town, I had to go for the tacos on my first visit. I tried three pork tacos ($10), which were flavorful due to the pineapple topping. However, they were extremely greasy and not even the double corn tortillas (which weren't really toasted or very warm) would hold a full taco together.

My wife and I ordered the chips, salsa, and guac (~$10) to share, and portion wise, it's a bit small. I would likely not get this again. While the chips were fresh, the guac is simply mashed avocados (no ingredients like onions, tomatoes, serrano peppers, garlic, etc.). The salsa was neither mild, medium, nor hot. It was more on the sweet side...

Great location and friendly staff, but there's not much seating if it's crowded. Seems like this is a spot where a lot of people order and take their meals to-go.

How far from the Vetri tree has this apple fallen and rolled, and rolled, and rolled...  We loved this place.  We spent a week eating dinner here every night, just for fun.  We took all our visiting friends here for lunch or dinner.  We got take out, we sat at that halfway tipped over table, we sweat ourselves into puddles on the benches out front on July lunch trips...blah blah blah...

We've been back about 10 times since Vetri sold the place and each time something is worse than before.  Smaller menu, louder and more irritating music, pizza taking too long...But service and food was always good.  This time the service was a mess.  

From the outside we thought the place was packed, and the staff was busting-ass to serve everybody.  There were parties on the sidewalk waiting to be called.  We almost went next door for tacos instead.  But when I went in, it wasn't crowded;  I got seated right away.  Or, I got seated right away when, having being ignored by the host for 5 minutes, I asked to put my name on the list. That was fine, though, because we got seated without having to wait to be called.  So it all worked out.

Anyway, I can forgive chaos and errors in a packed house with waiting crowds, but there were 9 seats available and the whole window counter was empty.  And the place was full of mellow customers.  I won't go through everything, but the general vibe was "we're under duress" and that came thru as rude at every contact point--not from the person who took our order, though, she was nice.  If we go back and it's like this again, I think we'll throw in the towel.

No fun, but the pizza was still good.

My wife and I ate there on a Friday night prior to going to a concert. Even though the food was okay, I was upset because of the apparent need to get us served and out so that they could seat another couple. It seemed like they were more concerned with how many meals they could serve that night. In additon, it was very cramped and parties of two are all over each other. I must have been hit in the head at least twice by a waiter and a busboy trying to get to the table next to us. The tables are so small that my dish with my entree on it was hanging half off of the table because the tables are too small to accomodate 2 people and bread and water and wine glasses, etc. I guess the smaller the table the more people that can be fed. Not a good idea!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I rarely ever write reviews, but ... Our experience here is making the former long-time restaurant worker in me speak up. The food ( we had a cheesesteak & a pizza steak) was good. Not amazing, but certainly tasty. But the atmosphere left much to be desired. We arrived at 9 pm, entering right after a family of four. The dining area is very small - maybe 10 small tables - so we chose a table a few over from the other family. A few minutes after we sat down with our drinks one of the staff members asked us to move to a table right next to the family,  even though all the other tables were empty and doing so crowded both of our parties, because he wanted to stack the chairs and sweep under the tables. While we waited for our food, four more parties came in and ordered --- and the guy didn't stop sweeping and stacking chairs! Customers were having to pull chairs out of the stacks just to have a place to sit! I get it that the staff were ready to leave, but they shouldn't have taken our money if they weren't willing to accommodate us. We felt very rushed and unwelcomed, and for that reason I do not recommend this place.

Stopped by for an early dinner on a Monday night without reservations. The hostess had to check with the co-owner and after 5 minutes we were seated at what seemed to be a nice quiet table for two. Little did we know the table of 4 next to us was reserved by a regular looking to show off to her friends. There was commotion, greetings by the owners, everyone standing up and talking, which encroached on our space. The owners came over frequently which was nice - always followed by loud talk - server bringing food - again very cramped. Never once did anyone have any regard for us - or either of the- owners inquiring about our meals or realizing there was any disruption to us. Food was great and so was the wait staff. It's too bad the owners did not appreciate our business or how the commotion with the other table impacted our dining experience.

Unfortunately, not as good as it's been in the past, and it pains me to say this, as I was really looking forward to dinner there. Very very cramped, way too many tables for the room, so jostling by fellow diners and wait staff was constant. Many tables out on the sidewalk, far too many for the staff to cover, so service, while polite, was way way way to rushed for our taste. 

Food was good, but for instance my appetizer was served long before my wife's, so my grilled octopus, while tasty and perfectly cooked, was room temperature by the time I started to eat. Other diners constantly apologizing for brushing past us while squeezing past the obviously too closely spaced tables made for a bit of embarrassment on their part. Having someone's legs and behind bumping you on the elbow while you lift your fork makes for a less than relaxing experience. Food: good, not great. Atmosphere: needs work. We'll come again, but will be sure to be seated along the wall so we don't feel like we're on an airliner sitting in coach near the toilet.

I went to dinner with three associates; based on a recommendation, and unfortunately I was highly disappointed. The place was nice looking but too cramped for my taste. It was a busy evening but I felt I welcomed. I actually felt bad for the workers because they have to climb up and door stairs and at times have to navigate the stairs with customers. The tables are also so cramped that you find yourself having to constantly squeezing into your seat to allow the workers to squeeze by. The food was just okay and nothing to write home about. It took over an hour and fifteen minutes to get our food and then I had to send my plate back because the food was just warm not hot. We kept getting what felt like forced apologise for the delays and nothing else. When we were greeted at the front door the folks in my party felt a little put off by the way we were greeted. I would never come back, nor would I recommend Ralphs Italian restaurant to any of my friends or associates.

Good for crowds.....

It's nice to have a family chain restaurant in the middle of the city.  Nice design as expected.  Huge place with large dining area.

It was crowded on a busy Saturday afternoon.  Didn't seem under staffed but service was at a crawl.  Although our server was really nice.  They placed us in an extended room (probably the private dining space).  

Weird that there was no music and we can hear all the other tables around us.  Asked to turn on some music to drown out some of the awkward silence and that never happened.  Oh well.  I just figured a good manager would know how to set the ambience though the establishment.  Where we were seated was probably an after thought.

Food.....it was ok.  Probably over priced for the entree that we ordered (some pasta, burger and appetizers).

Overall I still love this Chain because I feel comfortable enough to bring my kids here and not worry too much about their fussiness.

I was so excited to try this place but it was a bad experience from the start. We had a reservation but had to wait 20 minutes in the bitter cold to be seated. The reason we had to wait in the cold is because there is no place to stand inside without standing creepily close to someone's table. 

There were drapes blocking the entrance and I am assuming it was to block the cold from the entrance. Had the heavy drapes not been there, people can at least stand in the doorway and wait. There has got to be a wall heater that can heat that entryway and allow them to remove the curtain. 

Finally we were seated but it was this tiny cramped 2 top by the window. Not much food was going to fit on that table. Plus, right behind my husband was a poorly placed coat rack. The coats were literally touching my husband's back and that was even with us pulling the table closer towards me. Regardless, we were going to try. Within minutes, people had to crawl and reach over my husband's back to get their coats. Very disruptive. Not their faults, it was the fault of the restaurant for trying to fit too much stuff in a small space. Finally, we asked to be moved to another table. The server said nothing could be done because the two empty 4 tops already had reservations. 

So, we left. Between the frigid air blasting my husband through the front when the door opened and people reaching behind him for their coats, we had enough. Not going to spend that kind of money on dealing with that.

DO NOT GO! The management and wait staff made us feel incredibly uncomfortable.  Someone will come over every 5 minutes to try to take our plates away even though we were still eating.  It got to a point were several staff members hovered around our table.  We left without finishing our wine.  There were empty tables around us so the restaurant was not packed.

I've come here twice in the past month, once for lunch (ended up taking the food to go because there was no space) and another time for a drink. 

The space is tiny here, it's more enjoyable when it's not crowded. When ordering for lunch, it was awkward waiting for the order because there really isn't much room to stand without being in someone's way. I ordered the breakfast wrap but my two friends also ordered food that needed to be toasted and it took too long. The wrap itself was good, but really small....look how big my cookie was next to the burrito! The second time I came back, I was pretty sick and asked for a hot water but treated my friend to a drink here. Got a really weird look when they asked me if I was really ordering a hot water...I would rather go somewhere else in the area for a sandwich or drink in the future.

I had heard good things about this place but, truly, it is a tiny little hallway.  We went in there and it was jam packed, mega loud and total chaos.  I can't imagine how anyone would ever sit in there to eat unless maybe it was a weekday and totally dead and there were no customers.  If anyone came in to order and you were sitting at one of the table, they would be literally on top of you.  I have no idea about the food or drinks bc we left after a few minutes.

Can I give this a big fat zero?? Worst. Experience. Ever. I went once on a night during the week in the fall when it wasn't crowded and that was fine. BIG mistake to go at a time when you'd actually want to be outside. 

It's everyone for themselves to get a seat. So if you're sitting, people are staring you down and stalking you. If you're waiting, you probably want to bring brass knuckles to beat away your competition. 

And for some reason they have hostesses. When I expressed frustration, one cut me off and told me they have no say - clearly I was interfering with her "job". 

The customers dictate who gets the next table - so you could be waiting for an hour and loose a table to someone who already has one but is saving another for their  friends. 

Some places care about their customers - this one cares about their bottom line.

Often too crowded and has trouble-making crazy people inside.  I become impatient with things there like: this place made a tasty hamburger but they put salt on it plus the order taker talked crude.  Food would have tasted better without salt.

Came here for brunch with a friend on a Sunday. My friend had a reservation but when we got to the front, the woman who helped us was confused. She told us she was the owner's wife and not really a hostess but seated us anyway. I don't think she seated us at a table that was assigned to any wait staff because we sat there for twenty minutes with water she gave us and no one came by. 

The worst part of it was that we were seated right next to the bar and the wait staff kept congregating at the bar to socialize with each other. We clearly were ready to order and made eye contact with most of them but no one took the initiative to come help us. They kept coming to the table next to us and never stopped. 

The menu looked over priced and was small for brunch so we got up to leave. We stood there for a minute, paused to see if any one was going to come help. And they just looked at us. Very weird overall experience, I think there was a serious organizational problem that caused us to get overlooked, because it wasn't crowded and it seemed like there was plenty of staff.

Wait time was ridiculous food was ok warm not hot. Seating was limited to what seemed to be one area I like to relax with my family when we go out. I don't really care for crowded accommodations especially when more than half of the place is empty. And not reserved. It may be easier on servers. But how much more of a convenient option could it really be for them getting through such tight spots when serving. Prices were good. Place was clean. Servers have very big attitudes I guess short staffed.

I have to admit, I don't understand all the hype. It is certainly a beautiful space. And the food was above average. But the service was significantly lacking. The staff was young and lacked experience. I was seated at a small table and a lot of food came at once. I had a few things still yet to come, so I asked my server to please hold off on those items until I could catch up. For the record, I was not eating slowly. A minute later more food came and the runner stood by my table with the food in his hands and nowhere to put it. He told me there was a space issue. No kidding. He continued to stand there, I suppose he wanted me to somehow make room? I told him that I had asked the kitchen to slow down because I had no room, and he rushed away with the food. Moments later the manager came over and rudely insisted that all my food was meant to be eaten at the same time. When I explained that it was simply a space issue she curtly replied that "they would give me plenty of time then" and stormed away. Well, she made good on that promise. I didn't see anyone again for a half hour, or the rest of my food for 45 minutes. 

You can't expect guests to be able to control the pace of their food when ordering via an app. And you can't seat someone at a table too small to hold the food. And then when things go awry, you can't punish the guest for your mistakes. Overall my rating is poor because of the overall experience, service, and being treated rudely. At that point the food doesn't even matter. 

With egos like this you'd think the food was blowing your socks off, but it's not. It's good, but not worth the attitude. Save your money and go to Zahav.

用户希望的方向：lower

违反要求的英文含义：["The restaurant is crowded, packed, cramped, or extremely busy.", "There are too many people and very little space between customers."]

请从输入评论中恰好选择4条：2条明确满足要求，expected_direction=positive；2条明确违反要求，expected_direction=negative。每条评论最多使用一次。

要求：

1. query_text 必须是自然的中文找餐馆问题，只表达当前固定特征和指定方向。
2. query_text 不得出现商家名称、评论编号，也不得暗示已经知道答案。
3. requirement_text 用简短中文写清需要评论回答的要求。
4. evidence_span 必须逐字复制 review_text 中一段连续原文；不能翻译、改写、拼接或补字。
5. 原文必须能够直接证明正面或反面。泛泛的总体好评、差评、星级倾向和意思不清楚的句子不能使用。
6. 如果评论只提到相邻概念但不能证明当前特征，不要选择。

8. 证据必须直接说明商家确实满足或违反要求。仅仅说“A比B更好/更差”、假设以后会怎样、或者只有在某个未满足条件下才成立，都不能当作明确证据。

      "expected_direction": "positive或negative",
      "evidence_span": "从对应review_text逐字复制的连续原文"
    }
  ]
}

drafts必须恰好有4项，且必须是2项positive和2项negative。
